text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: service=metrics-log-ingest, alert=log-forwarder-backpress, urgency=high. PD link: https://pagerduty.example/INCIDENTS/PD12345 :rotating_light:

maria: acked the PD page. I'm looking now. any customer-facing symptoms?

alex: seeing heavy consumer lag on the log-forwarder topic, single shard blowing up. dashboards show consumer_lag_total > 1e6 for shard-7.

ryan: ugh. that shard hosts high-volume ingestion from mobile telemetry. customers might see missing events and delayed dashboards.

maria: thanks. can we triage whether it's consumer slowness vs broker slowdown? alex, can you paste the kafkacat / consumer lag query?

alex: pasted quick query: `kubectl exec -n ingest deploy/log-forwarder -- kafka-consumer-groups --describe --group log-forwarder --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092`

alex: short results: shard-7 lag = 1,230,456; consumer state = REBALANCING; consumer pods for forwarder-7 are OOMKilled and restarting frequently. logs show GC spikes and TLS handshake timeouts.

maria: ok. sounds like consumer pod instability. steps: (1) scale up forwarder replicas for shard-7; (2) roll consumer JVM to reduced heap / disable some encoders; (3) enable fallback buffering to S3 for that tenant group.

ryan: I can scale now. `kubectl -n ingest scale deploy/log-forwarder --replicas=6 --selector=shard=7` (will run in 30s).

pagerbot: @maria scaled log-forwarder/shard-7 -> replicas 3 => 6 (action by ryan).

maria: nice. also bump JVM flags to `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=60 -XX:+UseG1GC` and restart one pod at a time. I'm preparing a quick patch to the StatefulSet config.

alex: one pod already restarted and rejoined, lag dropped ~300k. still high but moving.

pagerduty: Alert acknowledged by maria (on-call). Escalation policy paused while engineers triage.

maria: temporary mitigation in place. customer impact: dashboards delayed ~15-60m for a subset of customers on EU region ingest. Not blocking writes, writes are accepted but processing backlog grows. Filed interim customer note to #customer-ops: "We’re mitigating ingestion backlog; dashboards may be delayed. We'll update in 1h."

ryan: I'm tailing logs from the restarted pod. seeing repeated `Connection reset by peer` to Redis cache used for prefix dedupe. might be network flakiness between ingest nodes and cache cluster.

alex: ok add that too. if Redis is flapping, client retries are piling up and saturating consumer CPU. can we divert dedupe to local in-memory for now?

maria: create a canary config: set DEDUPE_MODE=local for shard-7 via patch: ```kubectl patch deploy/log-forwarder -n ingest -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"forwarder","env":[{"name":"DEDUPE_MODE","value":"local"}],"resources":{"limits":{"memory":"2Gi"}}}]}}}}'``` Apply to one pod at a time.

ryan: applied to forwarder-7-1; pod restarted and came up. CPU now lower on that pod, lag dropping another ~200k.

alex: good signal. plan: continue rolling dedupe change across remaining forwarder pods for shard-7, monitor lag; scale kafka consumers further if needed; open a pager to infra-net if Redis continues to show errors.

maria: agreed. I'll keep PD suppressed while we finish mitigation. can someone own customer comms and timeline?

ryan: I'll ping customer-ops and update the note with ETA: "mitigations in progress; expected backlog drain in 45–90 minutes; follow-up postmortem to come."

pagerbot: incident-bot note: mitigation actions in thread. remember to run `sre/incidents/create` after stabilizing to capture timeline.

maria: when we stabilize, open an incident ticket and assign to eng-sre for postmortem. initial impact: partial metric loss and dashboard delays for ~3% of active customers in EU. root cause hypothesis: combined Redis flapping + JVM memory config causing consumer churn and backlog.

alex: for follow-up: add circuit breakers around Redis dedupe, add client-side backpressure and increase consumer memory limits, and add a separate S3 fallback queue per shard to avoid cross-shard amplification.

ryan: noting runbook updates: add a quick command to flip DEDUPE_MODE to local per-shard, and a monitoring alert for consumer OOM rate > 1/min.

maria: thanks team. continuing to monitor. will post final stabilization and timeline here. :thumbsup:

(10:07) alex: lag trending down to ~120k, consumer restarts less frequent.

(10:12) maria: stabilized. marking last_message_ts=2790012920. follow-ups: postmortem owner = alex, follow-up ticket ID TKT-4521.
